 Guadalajara enters this match having won back-to-back Liga MX games, including a road victory over CF Monterrey, and the Chivas carry the kind of momentum that makes them dangerous at home. Sitting eighth in the table with 11 points and a neutral goal differential, they are a team finding their footing at the right time. Ricardo Marin leads the attack with five goals on the season, and the creative engine behind him — Roberto Alvarado with 14 chances created and 11 shots on target — gives Guadalajara multiple ways to hurt an opponent.
 Atlante arrives in a different kind of fight. The Potros are 11th with 7 points and a goal differential of -3, but they are not without weapons. Luis Calzadilla has been their most dangerous forward, with 3 goals and 12 shots on target. Martin Sarrafiore leads the squad with 18 chances created, and Jhojan Julio has quietly built a four-assist campaign that keeps defenses honest.
 This is a game where Guadalajara’s home form meets an Atlante side that has shown it can grind out results on the road. The tension between those two realities is what makes this worth watching closely.

 Game Preview
 Guadalajara sits eighth in Liga MX with 11 points, while Atlante occupies 11th with 7 points and a goal differential of -3 that reflects a side that has been outscored more often than not. The gap between these clubs in the table is real, but it is not insurmountable in a single match. For Atlante, a result here would do more than add points — it would signal that the gap between them and the upper half of the table is closeable. For Guadalajara, protecting home ground while pushing toward the top half of the standings gives this game genuine weight on both sides.
 What to Watch For
 Ricardo Marin is the player Atlante’s defense must account for first. Five goals in seven matches makes him the most productive striker in this fixture, and with Brian Gutierrez (2 assists, 14 chances created) and Roberto Alvarado (14 chances created) supplying the attack, Guadalajara has the personnel to expose a defense that has been leaking goals. Santiago Sandoval Gonzalez adds another dimension with 3 goals and 7 shots on target — a secondary threat capable of punishing any lapse in concentration.
 For Atlante, the question is whether Luis Calzadilla can find the net against a Guadalajara side that has conceded just once in their last two matches. Calzadilla’s 12 shots on target show he is getting into positions — converting them here would be significant. Alongside him, Walter Portales has contributed 1 goal, 2 assists, and 13 chances created, making him one of the more complete attacking contributors on the Atlante roster. If Jhojan Julio’s four assists translate into service, Atlante has the pieces to make this uncomfortable for the home side.
